_meta.title: Ephaptic / endogenous near-field properties — locked, cited measured inputs for neuro §19
_meta.what: Three independent measured anchors that pin the ABSOLUTE near-field magnitude §15/§18 left as [O] (alpha_em) and let the induced membrane polarization be DERIVED, not asserted.
_meta.derivation: induced somatic polarization dVm = (Bikson 2004 sensitivity) x (Frohlich&McCormick 2010 endogenous field); validated by CONTAINMENT in Anastassiou 2011's independently-measured <0.5 mV.
_meta.validated_claim: the endogenous cortical near-field is AT the measured ephaptic-effect threshold (dVm ~0.275 mV, contained in Anastassiou <0.5 mV; entrainment threshold within the endogenous range) - it is NOT negligibly weak. This CORRECTS the '§18 incidental EEG field is weak' framing (which is true only of the SCALP signal).
_meta.open_O: the ABSOLUTE field in the package's own dimensionless §18 units (= the measured-input alpha_em); the in-vitro(0.87)/in-vivo(2.29) state dependence; whether the measured spike-timing entrainment is FUNCTIONALLY USED by cognition (-> Mind).
_meta.retired_unchanged: the FAR-field radiative carrier stays retired (radiated fraction ~1e-16, §18 PART 0); light-speed axon stays retired; coherent radiative broadcast stays retired (tissue decoherence). §19 concerns ONLY the quasi-static NEAR field (instantaneous, 1/r^3, local) - orthogonal to the radiative claims.
_meta.payload_sha256_note: sha256 over json.dumps(measured, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':')) - the §19 module asserts this on load; any silent edit fails the gate.

frohlich_mccormick_2010.entrainment_threshold_note: weak EFs enhance and entrain the neocortical slow oscillation with an amplitude threshold WITHIN the range of in-vivo endogenous field strengths (i.e. the endogenous field sits at, not below, the entraining threshold)

bikson_2004.ref: Bikson M, Inoue M, Akiyama H, Deans JK, Fox JE, Miyakawa H, Jefferys JGR (2004) J Physiol 557(Pt 1):175-190
bikson_2004.note: uniform DC field parallel to somato-dendritic axis; field->somatic polarization is LINEAR at 0.12 +/- 0.05 mV per (mV/mm)

anastassiou_2011.ref: Anastassiou CA, Perin R, Markram H, Koch C (2011) Nat Neurosci 14(2):217-223
anastassiou_2011.note: extracellular fields induced ephaptically-mediated somatic dVm < 0.5 mV under subthreshold conditions; despite the small size these fields strongly ENTRAIN spike timing, particularly for slow oscillations

buzsaki_anastassiou_koch_2012.ref: Buzsaki G, Anastassiou CA, Koch C (2012) Nat Rev Neurosci 13(6):407-420 (origin of EEG/ECoG/LFP/spikes)
buzsaki_anastassiou_koch_2012.note: canonical account: scalp EEG is the volume-conducted, strongly attenuated far signal; the LFP near the sources is orders of magnitude larger. 'EEG is weak' refers to the SCALP signal, not the local near-field.
